skill: Translate a displayed linear system into its augmented matrix, preserving equation order and the natural x,y,z variable order.
learner_operation: For each displayed equation, collect variable terms on the left and constants on the right without scaling the equation; identify implicit unit and missing zero coefficients; select the matrix whose coefficient columns and final constant column match every row.
reasoning_steps: Read equation and natural variable order
Move terms across equality with sign changes where necessary
Supply implicit unit and missing zero coefficients
Form coefficient matrix in equation order
Append right-hand constants and select one of five matrix choices
response_contract: All ten assessed source questions use one radio selection from five complete math matrix choices. Canonical example has a worked solution but no answer field.
difficulty: Five easy sources have two equations in x,y (already ordered, missing-variable, or elementary rearrangement); five moderate sources have two or three equations in x,y,z. Requested easy should preserve the two-row, two-variable workload.
invariants: Coefficient columns followed by right-hand constants
Single correct radio choice and five-choice source bank
No solving system, row reduction, equation scaling, or new variable-name skill
essential_constraints: The correct matrix must represent left-minus-right variable coefficients and right-minus-left constants in each original equation
Explanations must follow organization, coefficient matrix, then augmentation
incidental_assignments: Which row or variable is absent
Which coefficient or constant a distractor corrupts
permitted_variations: Small signed integer coefficients and constants, including implicit +/-1
Same-method distributions of missing variables across rows and columns
Term order and side of equality within elementary easy workload
Correct option position and distractor error location
Equivalent irrelevant presentation spacing or term-order changes that preserve collected equations
